title: Q-Pilot: Field Programmable Qubit Array Compilation with Flying Ancillas
problem: FPQA with dynamic qubit connectivity enables cost-effective long-range gates but poses new compilation challenges requiring novel routing and mapping strategies. Fixed-connectivity compilation approaches do not exploit the dynamic movement capabilities of neutral atom arrays.
motivation: FPQA shows strong promise for quantum computing with dynamic qubit connectivity, but efficient compilation strategies are critical for practical quantum system deployment.
method: Q-Pilot is a router inspired by FPGA compilation that leverages flying ancillas (movable auxiliary qubits) to implement 2-qubit gates between data qubits mapped to fixed atoms. It employs domain-specific routing techniques optimized for dynamic qubit connectivity in neutral atom arrays to reduce circuit depth through strategic ancilla placement and movement.
key_novelty: Using flying ancillas as a compilation strategy for FPQA, enabling dynamic movement of auxiliary qubits to implement gates between fixed data qubits.
contributions: Q-Pilot router adapting FPGA compilation strategies to quantum computing with neutral atom arrays
Domain-specific routing techniques for FPQA with dynamic qubit connectivity
Demonstrated 1.4-27.7x circuit depth reductions across random, simulation, and QAOA quantum workloads
